_meta.status: PROVISIONAL: every number is chosen for what a player feels and is a first proposal to play; nothing is fitted to a percentage, a line or a ceiling
_meta.rulings: 00-rulings.md A1 to A3, A8, B15, C19, D24, D25, D28, F36, F38
_meta.clock: Hours and the squad's level by map are pacing.json's (ruling 36: one clock); this file reads them and types none.
_meta.read_by: tools/balance/check.py checks (b) and (e); python tools/balance/check.py --tables hits world budget

tiers_rule.why: A tier's HP and armour take the one factor (ruling A1); its damage factor takes 1.28 so a same-level Soldier's service-rifle hit lands the frail character in about four hits at every level, the count the charter asks (the enemy_damage column carries the growth).

tiers.about: The level-1 tier rows (enemies.json items[]). hp, armour, damage and attack_bonus are today's rows, read; the rule above moves them. Defense is fixed by tier and never grows (ruling A3); pressure_off is ruling 19's Pressure offset; lag is the levels a tier stands under its place's level; bulk and pressure are its cost in Soldier-equivalents (survival.json tiers).

vermin.why: a rat is hit by anyone who aims at it; a swarm stands a level under its masters, so more of them fit the room

minion.why: a minion is a level under the line it runs with, and easier to hit than a soldier

soldier.why: the unit every fight is counted in: at the place's level, Defense 11 (a Standard TN less one)

elite.why: an Elite is harder to hit (14), so it takes more of a squad's turns than its HP says (bulk 2.1 read again for Defense 14); it shakes off one pip of the best shooter's Reach

boss.why: a Boss is the hardest to hit (15): bulk 7.9 read again for it; it shakes off two pips

enemy_weapon.why: the foe's hit the hit tables count: the line's service rifle (weapons.json), in a tier's hands x its damage factor x enemy_damage

stated_attacker.about: Whom the enemy HP column is written for (the charter: a specialist in the grade one step under the map's best). Its points follow pacing.gates.ceiling_by_level (attribute and alpha at the ceiling); its grade is one under the finds grade of the map where the squad is at that level (pacing.grades_by_map); its ordinary sum is what a sheet carries without a cash-out (perks and passives that touch a plain hit).
stated_attacker.min_exchanges_why: a same-level foe survives the hardest plain blow on the sheet even with one Margin on it, so every foe takes a second blow (the maul specialist's Soldier falls to its second blow at every level, the rifle's to its third: --tables hits)

builds.why: the two-handed Strength specialist, the hardest plain blow on the sheet
the plain shooter, Agility and Dexterity

stated_attacker.why: a same-level foe that falls to one plain blow is not a fight (ruling A1 keeps today's counts; check (b) fails under min_exchanges)

stated_defender.about: Whom the enemy damage column is written for: the frail character in Light armour, and the hardy in Medium, against same-level foes.
stated_defender.min_exchanges_why: the frail character survives two blows of any same-level foe, a Boss's included: it always has one turn to answer

levels.about: An enemy's level comes from the map and the row, never from the party (ruling 24). Rows 1 to 7 are early, 9 to 14 late; the gate Elite (row 8), every Elite node and the vault's guard take the top; the Boss at row 15. A tier then stands its lag under the row's level. Everything is capped at the enemy table's top.
levels.fight_level_why: a fight of mixed levels is the level of its highest Elite or Boss if one stands, else its foes' (critic-consistency-2 6.5: the tier names are data, read by the XP and drill sites)

maps.about: Survival's five maps (the run's stage 1 to 5). Each map adds what it asks of the squad: templates that open there (from_stage, beside today's from_depth) and the tags its foes carry by tier.

1.kit: aim, cover and focus fire; the gate Elite and the Boss carry plates, so the Guard door is met once before it is learned
1.why: the first map is two levels and the class: its Boss stands at the level a squad that walked it holds

2.kit: spotting and flanks: skulking minions, and Soldiers that Suppress
2.why: two levels a map, the Boss at the map's top (2m + 1)

3.kit: spread out against FIRE, kill the healer first, break or respect the Bonds
3.why: casters arrive with Masterwork's first finds, so a squad meets the words when it can answer them

4.kit: armour-piercing and the big cash-out, Slam plates, Rebuke prayers
4.why: the second half of Survival: the line itself carries plates

5.kit: all of it at once, then the final boss
5.why: the final map: its Boss is the final boss, one level over a squad that reaches it at the level map 5's gate gave (pacing.levels.lands)

final_boss.account_reward_text: Kept for when accounts exist (the charter: not in 0.34)
final_boss.after: the boon of three as after every Boss, the Survival cleared panel with the run's score, then retire or walk on into endless
final_boss.why: it asks for everything the five maps taught: plates, words, the line held against FIRE, Bonds that pull a runner back, and a cash-out saved for the turn its plates are down

endless.levels_why: one level a map (ruling 24): each endless map is a level for you and a level for them, until foes stop at the table's top

past_cap.why: from the first map whose every foe is at the top, each map puts a little more in the room (about one more Soldier in a four-squad's plain fight every two maps); before it, the foes' levels are the growth

6.asks: plates on the line: armour-piercing, Slam, a cash-out for a plate-less turn

10.asks: a runner is Tugged back: break the Bond or fight in its reach

13.asks: the final boss again, at the map's level

endless.kits_repeat: after map 13 the list starts again at map 6's, each tag one step stronger, to _iii
endless.boon_cap: the boon cap stays (ruling A10, scale.caps.items.boon_cap); a boon past it is worth nothing and its card says so (critic-consistency minor 6)

budget.about: The fight budget for a squad of 1 to 4, in Soldier-equivalents. Bulk = bulk_per_char_round x n x rounds; pressure = pressure_per_char[n - 1] x n x the kind's pressure_kind; a foe costs its tier's bulk and pressure x lag_factor ** (squad level - foe level), an Elite and a Boss x their share by squad (survival.json share). The party's level is used for this alone.
budget.lag_factor_why: a foe one level over takes about two fifths longer to drop and hits about a third harder on the columns: it fills the room like 1.4 foes of your level (x1.39)

light.node: a plain fight at row 1 or 2; a campaign's easy
light.why: the first fights of a map are a warm-up

hard.node: an Elite, the gate, the vault's guard (x its guard_factor)
hard.why: an Elite's room hurts more each round, so it is felt in the first exchange, not the sixth

final.why: the last fight of Survival most

budget.boss_alone: Ruling 38: a four-player Boss comes alone when its own cost fills the deadly room (at the four-player share its bulk is inside the room's band); kept as it falls, read by the run simulator after the build. --tables budget prints it.
budget.map_term: the map term (survival.json stage.bulk, stage.pressure) counts from endless.past_cap.from_map only

enemy_doors.about: An enemy's door reads the same ladder as a character's, at its door points and its level: a tag at a Reach step carries the family that step needs (ruling 13). Plates soak on enemy_armour; amounts dealt through a door read enemy_damage; casters' Line length and top stage come from Brain Power and Will Power in their door blocks (the casters' typed max_words and reach_bonus go).
enemy_doors.casters_why: each caster keeps today's Line length or top stage by reading the ladder at those points; a Soldier's heart fills to three, an Elite's to four, a Boss's to five, as a player's would
enemy_doors.faith_reads: the highest Devotion and Faith across a row's door blocks (today the last block wins, combat.ts:675)
enemy_doors.mp: a soul caster's mp (enemies.json soul_casters[].mp) is its level-1 pool, x scale.columns.mp at its level

fields.tier: top level: one of pacing.xp.campaign_tiers' ids
fields.levels: top level: {start, end}, checked against the tier's row
fields.zone_level: each zone: the place's level; every fight in the zone with no level given takes it, then the Narrator's shift
fields.act_level: each act, optional: a band {from, to} its zones are checked against

campaign.fallback: the party's level, with a validator warning, only for a file with no level anywhere (ruling 28)

m813.why: the first fight is at your level; the ramp a level up as the guns turn on you; station security the level you should have grown to by the end
